subject: Hosted→Dedicated: capacity matrix review & switchover timetable
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@ledger.ai>, Anna Lopez <anna@ledger.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted→Dedicated: capacity matrix review & switchover timetable

Hi Sam / Anna —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Attached is the initial capacity matrix we discussed (ledger-capacity-matrix-v1.xlsx). Before we lock dates for the Hosted→Dedicated migration we need a short sizing validation pass so our Dedicated fleet allocation matches your production workload. Can you please confirm the following by EOD Friday so we can finalize the staging window?

- 99th percentile sequence length (tokens) for your longest workflows (billing and doc ingestion).
- Average and peak QPS (requests/sec) by route (chat vs. embedding vs. rerank).
- Percent of requests that use tool-calls / function-calling (affects context size).
- Expected production concurrency per region (US primary, EU secondary).
- Any hard SLA targets (p50/p95 latency goals) we should honor during acceptance testing.

What we will do once we get those numbers: plug them into the capacity matrix to produce a recommended GPU profile (instance types + counts), define the staging load tests, and propose a 48–72 hour acceptance window. Our typical acceptance criteria: throughput at commit >= 95% of baseline, p95 latency within agreed SLO, and no functional regressions on your core prompt sets.

Proposed go-live windows (open for negotiation):
- Dec 21–22: light business day window (preferred)
- Jan 05–06: post-holiday fallback window

Attachments: ledger-capacity-matrix-v1.xlsx, onboarding-runbook-v2.pdf (draft)

Next steps: once we have your numbers, Neha will map to GPU families and propose a rehearsal schedule.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks, sending the numbers below (pulled from last 30 days):

- 99th percentile sequence: 3,200 tokens (billing flows spike to ~5k during heavy ingestion).
- Avg QPS: 12 rps overall; peak sustained bursts to 85 rps for short windows (~10–15 minutes).
- Tool-calls: ~18% of chat requests trigger function calls; embeddings are ~22% of traffic.
- Concurrency by region: US: 90% of traffic, EU: 10% (we plan EU read-only for now).
- SLA targets: p95 < 1.2s for chat generate, p95 < 300ms for embedding.

Procurement timeline: procurement@ledger.ai has started a PO draft (ledger-po-draft.pdf). Legal will review the SOW next week. We can target Dec 21 as a go/no-go if Redwood provides the final staging plan by Monday.

- Sam

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sam Patel <sam@ledger.ai>, Anna Lopez <anna@ledger.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated: capacity matrix review & switchover timetable

Thanks for the numbers, Sam — these are helpful. I've ingested the profile into the matrix and sketched a proposed mapping. Highlights and proposed gating for staging: 

1) Suggested GPU mix (based on token length distribution + peak bursts):
   - 4 x A100-80GB for model serving (primary) — handles long sequences (up to 5k tokens).
   - 8 x A100-40GB for steady-state concurrency and batching (embeddings + rerank).
   - 2 x spare T4 nodes for low-cost burst absorb and warm-cache population.

2) Autoscale & routing policy:
   - Conservative min replicas to preserve cold-start profile (min=4), target-scale to meet 95th percentile concurrency.
   - Route latency-sensitive endpoints (embeddings) to dedicated 40GB pool to preserve p95 < 300ms.

3) Staging runbook (summary):
   - Day -4: provisioning and baseline smoke — confirm image, model version, quantization profile.
   - Day -3: KV/prefix cache warm-up using replayed production traces (2x replay over 3 hours).
   - Day -2: soak tests at 50–70% expected peak (4 hours) + functional smoke on prompt sets.
   - Day -1: peak load test (90%–110% bursts) for 2 hours, run token-cost comparison and leakage checks.
   - Day 0 (cutover rehearsal): canary 10% routing -> 30% -> 100% if SLA holds. Keep automatic fallback to Hosted for first 3 hours.

4) Acceptance criteria (must pass all):
   - Throughput: sustained >= 95% of hosted baseline under equivalent traffic profile.
   - Latency: p95 <= target SLOs for each route.
   - Correctness: no prompt-set regressions; sample evaluations must pass golden set.
   - Cost delta: projected tokens/unit cost not higher than 10% above target estimate (we'll run token-cost simulation during Day -1 tests).

5) Operational needs / on-call:
   - Redwood SRE on-call for cutover + 72 hours post-cutover (Neha + one infra lead).
   - Ledger to assign a technic rep for live debugging and a procurement contact for escalation.

I'll attach a short onboarding-runbook-v2.pdf with the full checklist and command snippets. Karthik, can you confirm the model bundle we should preload (release tag) and whether Ledger wants quantization enabled by default?

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated: capacity matrix review & switchover timetable

Sam / Anna —

This looks good. Neha's staging plan covers the key gates. Proposed next steps and schedule:

- Mon Dec 14: Redwood finalizes capacity allocation and posts a rehearsals calendar (Day -4 to Day 0).
- Tue Dec 15: preflight provisioning (we'll provision the A100-80/40 pools, install model bundle).
- Thu Dec 17: run replay warm-up and initial soak tests.
- Sat Dec 19: full peak load rehearsal (rehearsal run #1).
- Mon Dec 21 (preferred): canary->cutover window. We keep auto-fallback to Hosted for first 3 hours and hold a rollback window until 23:59 PST.

Acceptance tests for the rehearsal and Day 0:
- Load generator script: run 2x replay for 3 hours and a 90% burst run for 1 hour.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency per route, token-cost delta, error rate, model output sampling for correctness.
- Post-cutover rollback criteria: any sustained p95 > 1.5x agreed SLO, or any regression failing the golden prompt set.

Operational ask: Ledger to provide a single Slack escalation channel + a named on-call contact for Day 0. Redwood will provide SRE and an eng lead for the 48 hours post-cutover.

Please reply with explicit "ACK" on the timeline and the on-call contact. If we get ACK by EOD Tue Dec 15, we'll proceed to provision.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
